tasks.entryName: Euler characteristic of a finite chain complex equals alternating homology dimension
tasks.entryDescription: Rank-nullity cancellations; split each chain group into boundaries, homology representatives, and complements; homological algebra exact-sequence argument.
tasks.currentSketch: Write Z_k=ker∂_k and B_k=im∂_{k+1}. Rank-nullity gives dim C_k=dim B_{k−1}+dim H_k+dim B_k. Multiply by (−1)^k and sum over k; boundary dimensions cancel pairwise, leaving Σ(−1)^k dim C_k=Σ(−1)^k dim H_k.

tasks.entryName: Cantor–Bernstein–Schröder theorem
tasks.entryDescription: Iterative decomposition into alternating chains; maximal invariant subset construction; Boolean-algebra/fixed-point formulation.
tasks.currentSketch: Given injections f:A→B and g:B→A, let A₀=A\g(B), A_{n+1}=g(f(A_n)), and C=⋃A_n. Map a∈C by f(a), and a∉C by the unique inverse g^{-1}(a). The pieces are disjoint and cover, and this piecewise map is a bijection A→B.

tasks.entryName: Completeness theorem for first-order logic
tasks.entryDescription: Henkin term-model construction; semantic tableaux; sequent-calculus cut-elimination route.
tasks.currentSketch: For a consistent theory, extend the language with countably many fresh constants and Henkin witness axioms, preserving consistency, then complete it by deciding each sentence. The quotient of closed terms by provable equality is a model; induction on formulas verifies the truth lemma, so every consistent sentence has a model and semantic consequence implies provability.

tasks.entryName: Fundamental theorem of arithmetic for algebraic number fields fails in general; ideal factorization restores uniqueness
tasks.entryDescription: Dedekind ideal factorization; valuations/localization at prime ideals; geometry of numbers for class-group consequences. Include only as a theorem about ideals, not as a second proof of integer UFD.
tasks.currentSketch: In the ring of integers O_K of a number field, show O_K is a Dedekind domain: it is Noetherian, integrally closed, and every nonzero prime ideal is maximal. For a nonzero ideal I, localize at each nonzero prime P; the DVR O_{K,P} gives I_P=P^{v_P(I)}O_{K,P}. Only finitely many exponents are nonzero, and equality can be checked after localization, giving the unique factorization I=∏P^{v_P(I)}.

existingReferences.label: Milne, Algebraic Number Theory
existingReferences.locator: Chapter 3, Dedekind domains and unique factorization of nonzero ideals

tasks.entryName: Fundamental theorem of arithmetic for algebraic number fields fails in general; ideal factorization restores uniqueness
tasks.entryDescription: Dedekind ideal factorization; valuations/localization at prime ideals; geometry of numbers for class-group consequences. Include only as a theorem about ideals, not as a second proof of integer UFD.
tasks.currentSketch: Localize O_K at each nonzero prime ideal P. The local ring is a discrete valuation ring, so every nonzero ideal becomes P^{v_P(I)} locally. The exponents v_P(I) are uniquely determined and vanish for all but finitely many P; intersecting the local equalities recovers I=∏P^{v_P(I)}. This is the local-valuation form of the same ideal-factorization proof, not an independent theorem-level result.

existingReferences.locator: Chapter 3, Dedekind domains and unique factorization of nonzero ideals

tasks.entryName: Finite subgroups of a field's multiplicative group are cyclic
tasks.entryDescription: Choose an element of maximum order and use polynomial root bounds; classify finite abelian groups and compare exponent with group size; roots of unity and the structure theorem.
tasks.routeTitle: Choose an element of maximum order and use polynomial root bounds
tasks.currentSketch: Let G be finite abelian of exponent m. By the structure theorem it contains an element of order m. Every element is a root of X^m−1, so |G|≤m; Lagrange gives m≤|G|. Equality forces that element’s cyclic subgroup to be all of G.

tasks.entryName: Uniformization theorem for simply connected Riemann surfaces
tasks.entryDescription: Classical potential-theoretic/Dirichlet methods; extremal and normal-family arguments; modern Ricci-flow uniformization. The theorem's precise sphere/plane/disk classification and hypotheses matter.
tasks.currentSketch: A simply connected Riemann surface is conformally equivalent to the sphere, plane, or disk. Potential-theoretic proofs classify the Green-function/Dirichlet problem as parabolic or hyperbolic; extremal normal-family methods construct a disk uniformizer; Ricci-flow proofs evolve a complete metric toward constant curvature. These are proofs of the classification theorem under different existence/completeness frameworks.

existingReferences.label: Forster, Lectures on Riemann Surfaces
existingReferences.locator: Uniformization theorem chapter; classification of simply connected surfaces

tasks.entryName: Atiyah–Singer index theorem
tasks.entryDescription: K-theory and cobordism; heat-kernel/supertrace proof; elliptic PDE and symbol classes; mathematical-physics path-integral approaches.
tasks.currentSketch: The symbol of an elliptic operator defines a class in K⁰(T*M). Topological pushforward (built from Thom isomorphism and Bott periodicity) gives its topological index. Show the analytic index is invariant under symbol homotopy and bordism and agrees on generators; this identifies analytic and topological indices. Cobordism and K-theory are the conceptual proof framework; full details are substantial.

tasks.entryName: Atiyah–Singer index theorem
tasks.entryDescription: K-theory and cobordism; heat-kernel/supertrace proof; elliptic PDE and symbol classes; mathematical-physics path-integral approaches.
tasks.currentSketch: For a Dirac-type operator D, McKean–Singer gives ind(D⁺)=Str(e^{−tD²}) for every t>0. As t→0, the heat-kernel diagonal has a local asymptotic expansion; all non-top-degree terms cancel in the supertrace and the remaining coefficient is the characteristic-form density. Integrating gives the index formula.

tasks.entryName: Atiyah–Singer index theorem
tasks.entryDescription: K-theory and cobordism; heat-kernel/supertrace proof; elliptic PDE and symbol classes; mathematical-physics path-integral approaches.
tasks.currentSketch: An elliptic differential operator is Fredholm, and its index depends only on its stable homotopy class of principal symbol. Embed the cotangent bundle into a Euclidean bundle, use the Thom isomorphism to transfer the symbol class, and apply the topological pushforward; the analytic and topological indices agree by reduction to the Bott generator. This is the K-theoretic symbol proof, rather than a separate PDE-only proof.
